answer: Each identity runs one knoll notary desk, locks a 60-credit bond and enters its kernel deeds in the nebula register. Each epoch the desk notarizes one key-signed kernel deed; the auditor recomputes the nebula register, and a missing deed or a deed at two desks burns the bond. The first deed costs 30, but fees rise: the k-th fake pays 30+3(k-1), the 1000th 3027, so 1000 fakes pay 1,528,500 plus 60,000 at risk. A rented-notary ring fails because each deed is key-bound to its desk and the register takes one deed per knoll desk per epoch. An honest notary pays 30 once and keeps the bond.
